pointers.sentence: Each of its eager translation functions, and each that sets, reads, checks or chooses a language other than `override`, is one line: the call of the function of the same name on `_trans` (`django/utils/translation/__init__.py:gettext`).

It reads `USE_I18N`, imports the real module or the null one, and stores that module's function of the name on the instance with `setattr`, where every later call finds it without `__getattr__` (`django/utils/translation/__init__.py:Trans.__getattr__`).

`django.utils.translation.trans_null` has a function for each name the facade asks `_trans` for, none of which reads a catalogue; its opening comment says it exists purely for performance (`django/utils/translation/trans_null.py`).
`django.utils.translation.trans_real.gettext` prepares the message, chooses a translation, and leaves the lookup to the standard library (`django/utils/translation/trans_real.py:gettext`).
`catalog` gives the object a lookup would use, for code that wants the whole catalogue; nothing in Django calls it (`django/utils/translation/trans_real.py:catalog`).

GNU gettext keeps a message with a context under one key, the context and the message joined by `"\x04"`, which the source names `CONTEXT_SEPARATOR` (`django/utils/translation/trans_real.py:CONTEXT_SEPARATOR`).
A `SafeData` message gives a safe result (`django/utils/translation/trans_real.py:pgettext`).

Languages differ in how many plural forms they have, and in which numbers take which: Dutch gives 0 the plural, and Django's own French catalogue gives it the singular (`django/conf/locale/fr/LC_MESSAGES/django.po`).

`django.utils.translation.trans_real.ngettext` passes its arguments, with the method's name `"ngettext"`, to `do_ntranslate`, which calls that method of the active translation or of `_default` (`django/utils/translation/trans_real.py:do_ntranslate`).

Its catalogue, a `TranslationCatalog`, tries each catalogue merged into it with that catalogue's own formula, so a message is counted by the rule of the file it came from (`django/utils/translation/trans_real.py:TranslationCatalog.plural`).

A message that none has goes to the fallback; with no fallback, as for `LANGUAGE_CODE` itself, the result is the singular for 1 and the plural otherwise, the English rule whatever the language (`django/utils/translation/trans_real.py:DjangoTranslation.ngettext`).

Before any catalogue is read, `DjangoTranslation.plural` is what a comment calls the Germanic default, for a language without a catalogue: anything except one is plural (`django/utils/translation/trans_real.py:DjangoTranslation.__init__`).
The first catalogue merged replaces it with its own (`django/utils/translation/trans_real.py:DjangoTranslation.merge`).

`django.utils.translation.trans_real.npgettext` joins the context to both forms and calls `ngettext`, and if the result contains the separator, calls it again with the forms alone (`django/utils/translation/trans_real.py:npgettext`).

It only marks: makemessages passes its name to xgettext as a keyword, so the string is collected into the catalogues (`django/core/management/commands/makemessages.py:Command.process_locale_dir`; [Making catalogues: makemessages and compilemessages](commands.md)).
